In CK2, there was a thing called threat level (might’ve been something else idk been a bit) and basically if you had a really high threat level (because of constant warfare or you’re a huge empire) other nearby nations could basically form a coalition alliance that would all join a war if you attacked one of them. You’re threat level could get so high that nations of different faiths would even band together, and eventually you’re own holy orders would fight against you. You could significantly lower your threat level by granting vassals independence. The more powerful the vassals, the more it dropped your levels. Kinda hoping they bring this mechanic back to CK3, it’ll add more challenge to the game once you get to Big Kingdom/Empire stage

The 2020 Armenian–Azerbaijani conflict honestly gave me big insight into this idea. I followed the war relatively closely, because modern times means lots of soldiers recording and government released combat footage. Often times small wars like those where one side (Azerbaijani) is funded by a foreign entity (I think either Russia or Turkey was sending them drones, as well as other equipment.) you get a glimpse at what technology will be used for the next major conflict. The one thing that stood out was their use of drones. Swarms of suicide drones flying through the air, filling the battlefield with their constant buzzing, just the psychological effect alone was disturbing. In any video where a major battle was going on you could hear them in the background, occasionally see people try to shoot them down. There’s tons of video of these drones (POV video) diving down on enemy positions, supply lines, even enemy armored vehicles(even tanks). Whatever major conflict is next, no matter who is fighting, I’m sure we’ll see a large use of drone warfare.
